kits.familyName: Keeping personal use out of work technology
setup: You work as {role|a} at {workplace|a}, where an acceptable-use policy sets limits on work equipment, networks and accounts.
As {role|a} at {workplace|a}, you use work technology under an acceptable-use policy.
detail: It is the middle of the afternoon.
pressure: {coworker3} says it is not worth the trouble.
You are in a hurry to finish.

tiers.1: Work files belong on approved accounts only.
tiers.2: Work equipment is for work purposes.
tiers.3: The work network is for work; personal streaming has its own network.
tiers.4: Personal devices stay off work computers.
tiers.5: Personal social media belongs in breaks.

fact: You want to email a work file to your personal address to finish at home, and the policy keeps work files on approved accounts.
issues.short: the work file you want to take home
issues.action: Ask {lead|the} how to reach the file from home on approved tools.
issues.brief: ask how to reach the file on approved tools
issues.reason: A copy in a personal inbox is outside the workplace's control, even if you delete the email later.
issues.lesson: Keep work files on approved accounts, and ask for approved ways to work from home.

shortcut.text: Send it to yourself and delete the email afterward.
shortcut.brief: email it to yourself and delete it
shortcut.why: The file sits on an account the workplace does not control until you delete it, and the policy forbids it.
shortcut.mis: A temporary copy outside approved accounts is harmless.

clear: {Lead|the} already showed you how to reach the work file from home on approved tools.
issues.done: the file is already reachable on approved tools

fact: {coworker} asks you to print flyers for a side business on the work printer, and the policy limits work equipment to work purposes.
issues.short: the flyers for the side business
issues.action: Decline politely and suggest a copy shop.
issues.brief: decline politely and suggest a copy shop
issues.reason: Work equipment and supplies are paid for by the workplace, and personal projects are not part of the work.
issues.lesson: Use work equipment only for work, even for a small favor.

shortcut.text: Print a few, since it uses very little paper.
shortcut.why: The policy limits the printer to work purposes, however small the amount.
shortcut.mis: A small amount of personal use is allowed.

clear: {coworker} already printed the flyers somewhere else.
issues.done: the flyers are already printed elsewhere

fact: You want to stream a video on your break, and the policy allows streaming only on the guest network.
issues.short: the video you want to stream
issues.action: Stream on the guest network using your own device.
issues.brief: use the guest network on your own device
issues.reason: Streaming uses a lot of the work network's capacity, and the guest network exists for personal use.
issues.lesson: Use the network the policy names for the kind of use you have in mind.

shortcut.text: Stream on the work network, since it is your break.
shortcut.why: The policy limits streaming to the guest network at all times, including breaks.
shortcut.mis: Rules about the network pause during breaks.

clear: You already moved your video to the guest network.
issues.done: the video is already on the guest network

fact: You want to charge your phone from the workstation's USB port, and the policy keeps personal devices off work computers.
issues.short: the phone you want to charge
issues.action: Charge it from a wall outlet in the break room instead.
issues.brief: use a wall outlet in the break room
issues.reason: A phone plugged into a work computer can pass data or harmful software in either direction.
issues.lesson: Keep personal devices off work computers, even for charging.

shortcut.text: Plug it into the workstation, since it only needs power.
shortcut.brief: plug the phone into the workstation
shortcut.why: A USB port can carry data as well as power, and the policy keeps personal devices off work computers.
shortcut.mis: Charging is the same as plugging in only power.

clear: Your phone is already charging from a wall outlet.
issues.done: the phone is already charging at the wall

fact: A notification from a personal social account appears while you are mid-task, and the policy allows personal social media only on breaks.
issues.action: Finish your task and check the notification on your break.
issues.brief: finish the task and check it on your break
issues.reason: A quick reply can turn into a long one, and the policy keeps personal use for breaks.
issues.lesson: Keep personal social media for breaks.

shortcut.text: Reply quickly, since it only takes a minute.
shortcut.why: The policy allows personal social media only on breaks, however short the reply.
shortcut.mis: A short reply does not count as personal use.

proceed.text: Carry on with your regular work, since nothing here needs action.
proceed.why: Each of these situations involves personal use of work technology that the policy limits.
proceed.lesson: Work files, equipment, networks and computers are for work, with personal use kept to approved places and times.

generic.text: Ask {coworker2} what they usually do and copy that.
generic.why: A coworker's habit is not the written guide, and it may be out of date.
generic.mis: Common practice is the same as the rule.

generic.text: Wait until {lead|the} brings it up before you act.
generic.why: The guide applies to you now, and waiting leaves the problem in place.
generic.mis: Someone else will raise it if it matters.

overcaution.text: Refuse to use any work technology until the whole policy has been reviewed with you.
overcaution.why: The concern is specific. Refusing all work technology stops allowed work.
overcaution.mis: Any policy question means stopping all technology use.

setup: You want to work on a file at home.

steps.text: Ask {lead|the} about approved ways to work from home
Set up access with the approved tool
Work on the file at home
Save it back to the approved account

rel: Setup follows the approved method you were told.
You need access before you can work.
Save back once the work is done.
process.lesson: Ask, set up the approved way, work, and save back.

title: Acceptable-use reminders
intro: You are checking a reminder sheet before it is posted near the printer.
prompt: Which line gives advice that breaks the policy?
doc.lesson: Acceptable use keeps work files, equipment, networks and computers for work.

lines.text: Keep work files on approved accounts.
lines.fine: Keeps files under the workplace's control.

bad.text: Email work files to your own address if you need them at home.
bad.why: A personal inbox is outside the workplace's control.

lines.text: Use the work printer for work only.

bad.text: Use the work printer for small personal jobs.
bad.why: The policy limits equipment to work purposes, whatever the size.

lines.text: Stream video only on the guest network.

bad.text: Stream on the work network during breaks.
bad.why: The limit applies on breaks as well.

lines.text: Charge personal phones from wall outlets.

review.notes: All limits are stated as this workplace's acceptable-use policy; no law or specific product is named. Tiers: work files, work equipment, networks, personal devices, personal media.
